name: Ghost
tagline: Publishing and newsletters with no lock-in and no clutter
description: Ghost is a publishing platform for newsletters and blogs with memberships, built-in email delivery and a clean editor, and it can be self-hosted.
priceNote: Ghost(Pro) starts at $18/month billed yearly on the Starter plan and $29/month on Publisher, which is required for paid memberships; Business is $199/month and the price scales with audience size. Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Writers and small publishers who want newsletters without a page-builder tax
pros: Memberships and paid subscriptions work out of the box, which most newsletter tools bolt on
The editor is markdown-first, so posts live in plain text that a developer can read
Email delivery, segmentation and analytics are included rather than sold as add-ons
Self-hosting is genuinely supported, which removes lock-in for technical teams
cons: Ghost(Pro) pricing scales with audience size, so growing the list raises the bill
Theme customisation expects some HTML and CSS, which is a barrier for non-technical owners
There is no built-in ad network or plugin marketplace revenue split like WordPress offers
Fewer integrations than WordPress or a page builder, and a much smaller plugin ecosystem

features.name: Newsletters
features.detail: Built-in sending, segmentation, welcome sequences and email analytics

features.name: Memberships
features.detail: Paid subscriptions, tiers and member-only content without plugins

features.name: Markdown editor
features.detail: A fast, distraction-free editor with version history and restore

features.name: Self-hosting
features.detail: Run Ghost on your own infrastructure under the open-source licence

features.name: Themes and the app framework
features.detail: Custom themes plus an app framework for building your own features

features.name: Publishing API
features.detail: A documented API for headless setups and custom front ends

useCases: Run a paid newsletter for a niche audience with subscriptions handled end to end
Publish a company blog and newsletter without paying for a page-builder subscription
Let a technical founder self-host the newsletter so the content stays portable
Send a weekly client digest with segmented editions for different customer groups
bestForWho: Writers, coaches and small media businesses who want newsletter revenue without a heavyweight CMS.
verdict: Ghost is the tool I suggest to anyone whose main business is words, because the newsletter and the membership system are the product, not an add-on bolted onto a blog engine. The markdown editor means your posts stay in plain text, which matters the moment a developer touches the site or you decide to self-host. Email delivery, segmentation and analytics are included in the subscription, so you are not assembling a stack of four tools to charge for a newsletter. The two real drawbacks are the audience-based pricing, which rises as you succeed, and the fact that theming expects some HTML and CSS. Self-hosting is the escape hatch that makes the lock-in fear manageable, and for a paid newsletter or a company publication it is excellent value.
